title: Floquet-Weyl states at one-photon resonances in three-dimensional topological insulators
authors: Keiya Uehara, Ryo Okugawa, Takami Tohyama, Shun Okumura
abstract: Quantum materials exhibit exotic phases and electronic responses under irradiation by circularly polarized light, which breaks time-reversal symmetry and generates Floquet replica bands. Recently, Floquet topological states arising from direct resonances have attracted much attention, e.g., the emergence of Floquet-Weyl points at a one-photon resonance, rather than topological features within the modulated original bands via high-frequency expansion. In this study, we investigate the effects of a one-photon resonance in a representative three-dimensional topological insulator, Bi$_2$Se$_3$, applying Floquet theory under circularly polarized light. We find that four pairs of Floquet-Weyl points emerge in the intermediate-frequency regime, mediated by hybridization between the original and one-photon-resonant Floquet bands, preserving the threefold rotational symmetry of the crystalline structure. Our numerical calculations demonstrate that tuning the chemical potential via hole doping yields a large anomalous Hall conductivity, directly associated with these Floquet-Weyl points. This work provides a highly accessible route toward the experimental realization of one-photon-resonant Floquet-Weyl semimetals.
summary: The paper theoretically examines how driving a 3D Topological Insulator with circularly polarized light at one-photon resonance generates exotic Floquet-Weyl semimetallic phases. By analyzing the hybridization of electronic bands, the authors predict the emergence of Weyl points and show that this topological feature can be experimentally detected through a large anomalous Hall conductivity signal.
main_problem: The study investigates the emergence of Floquet-Weyl states in three-dimensional topological insulators when driven by circularly polarized light at a one-photon resonance.
main_result: Four pairs of Floquet-Weyl points are found to emerge due to hybridization between original and one-photon-resonant bands, leading to a large anomalous Hall conductivity tunable via hole doping.
method: The research employs Floquet theory combined with tight-binding modeling and numerical calculations to track the topological features in the quasienergy spectrum.
model_or_system: The system is based on $	ext{Bi}_2	ext{Se}_3$-type 3D Topological Insulators, modeled by an effective tight-binding Hamiltonian. The analysis utilizes Floquet theory for periodic driving by circularly polarized light (CPL).
key_observables: Floquet-Weyl points, anomalous Hall conductivity ($\sigma_{xy}$), and the topological phase diagram.
important_parameters: One-photon resonance condition, CPL amplitude ($E_0$), photon energy ($\Omega$), and chemical potential tuning via hole doping.
main_assumptions: The analysis focuses on the one-photon resonance mechanism, contrasting with high-frequency expansions; approximations are made in deriving the effective two-band Hamiltonian.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate schematics of CPL irradiation effects, nodal ring collapse to Weyl points, and comprehensive topological phase diagrams mapping out different Floquet states based on driving parameters.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the physical system ($	ext{Bi}_2	ext{Se}_3$ under CPL) to applying Floquet theory, deriving an effective Hamiltonian via canonical transformations, calculating the resulting Weyl points, and finally demonstrating the measurable consequence (AHC).
why_interesting: This work connects topological band theory with non-equilibrium quantum dynamics induced by light, which is highly relevant for understanding engineered quantum states in optical systems.
